name: Racing Yacht
instructions: omr/instructions/42074-1-1.pdf (book 1: the racing yacht; helm and rudder drive steps 10-21 and 38-44, winches and rubber bands steps 45-66, functions pages 80-81); 42074-1-2.pdf builds the alternate model

functions.does: The helm, a small steering wheel on the deck, turns the rudder at the stern: its 16 tooth gear drives, through a 16 tooth idler, a 16 tooth gear on the long shaft down the hull, whose 12 tooth bevel gear at the stern turns the 20 tooth bevel gear on the rudder's upright axle.
functions.source: book: steps 10-21 (the long shaft and gears), 38-44 (the stern bevel gears), page 81 (top insets: the helm turned, the rudder swinging)

functions.does: Either of the two winch cranks on the deck swings the boom and mainsail from side to side: a rubber band loop runs from each crank's reel to a reel in the middle, whose 8 tooth gear turns the 24 tooth gear at the foot of the boom.
functions.source: book: steps 45-66 (reels, rubber bands, 8 and 24 tooth gears), page 81 (lower inset: both cranks turned, the boom swinging)
functions.note: Turning one crank turns the other too, as the rubber bands join all three reels.

functions.does: The yacht stands on four small wheels under its hull, which roll freely so it can be pushed along a table.
functions.source: inferred: the wheels are built in at book steps 18-21 and the model has them; the book doesn't say what they are for

functions.does: The rubber bands slip if the boom is held, so the winches can't jam it.
functions.source: inferred: what rubber-band drives do; the book doesn't say
